Chapter 2, Verses 2.49-2.51 (Day 17)

Your right is to the work, not to the outcome. Sounds frustrating until you realize: outcomes were never in your hands anyway. All you ever had was this next action.

Chapter 2, Verses 2.71-2.72 (Day 24)

Wanting things doesn't make you alive - it makes you restless. The people who look most at peace aren't the ones who got everything they wanted. They're the ones who stopped wanting.

Chapter 3, Verses 3.37-3.39 (Day 53)

Think about the last thing you couldn't stop wanting. Notice how getting it didn't end the wanting; it just shifted to the next thing. Desire doesn't have a finish line.

Chapter 3, Verses 3.22-3.24 (Day 48)

What if you already had everything you think you're working toward - the security, the recognition, the freedom? Would you still do the work you're doing today?

Chapter 2, Verses 2.64-2.66 (Day 21)

The discipline isn't in controlling what you want. It's in not being controlled by it. You can want things. Just don't let the wanting run your life.

Chapter 2, Verses 2.40-2.42 (Day 14)

Half-efforts don't compound. A half-finished workout doesn't build muscle. A half-written book doesn't change anyone. The only effort that counts is the one you complete.

Chapter 3, Verses 3.25-3.27 (Day 49)

When you discover something that changes how you see the world, your first instinct is to tell everyone, to fix them. Don't. Let your life be the argument.

Chapter 3, Verses 3.31-3.33 (Day 51)

You collect insights like someone collecting receipts, nodding along, underlining passages, but never actually changing how you operate.

Chapter 2, Verses 2.60-2.63 (Day 20)

Constant thinking about something creates attachment. Attachment creates desire. Desire creates anger. Anger destroys clarity. Notice what you keep thinking about.

Chapter 4, Verses 4.07-4.09 (Day 58)

Something in you knows when you're living wrong - when you're faking it, avoiding what matters, coasting. The crisis isn't punishment. It's course correction.
